Programme policy · staging edition 1.0 · 11 November 2026

Partner Programme: Commercial & Payment Controls

Pre-activation notice. These published terms describe the intended programme for review. Submission of interest does not establish agency, employment or a commission entitlement. Only optional, manually issued TEST-ONLY pilot codes and buyer-confirmed attribution may be available on staging. After a buyer has registered a pilot code, the same buyer may voluntarily link a subsequent verified Razorpay test order for a non-payable demonstration. These isolated test records cannot generate real earnings or disbursements. A separate seven-check, staging-only onboarding status preview may also be available. It does not accept sensitive documents or activate real commissions. The final legally binding terms will be the signed partner agreement with the named contracting operator and current product schedule.

1. Scope and eligibility

Participation is free and available by invitation or application to independent, eligible India-based adults and businesses. Every application undergoes manual assessment for independence, legal restrictions, conflicts, product suitability and marketing methods. Approval requires a signed contract, tax/KYC verification and programme activation. The partner is an independent promoter of specifically approved software/digital products, not an authorised representative of the company, a statutory Committee, or a legal advocate through this programme.

2. Products for commission

Eligible products are those expressly designated in the partner's approved product schedule: approved POSH Navigator software access plans, online checklists, self-service digital compliance assessments and eligible digital guides. Certain upgrades or renewals may qualify only if paid within the first 12 months of the referred new customer's first verified paid order. Product availability and commissionability must be confirmed before referral.

Excluded: free Knowledge Library access, consultations or professional legal services, litigation/representation or advocate fees, statutory IC/LC appointments or inquiry assignments, government procurements/tenders, employer or Committee conflicts, independent training and audits, bespoke institutional engagements without a separate prior written lawful arrangement, manual cash sales and unapproved products.

3. Referral attribution

  1. Only an approved, active partner may use an issued referral code. One customer may have one credited partner. The first valid referral registered and accepted before checkout takes precedence, subject to independent review and corrections for proven abuse.
  2. A code or documented referral is eligible for up to 90 days before the customer's first verified paid purchase. Marketing clicks, visits, enquiries, screenshots or self-reported purchases alone do not create entitlement. The buyer must choose to use the referral identifier at checkout or confirm a compliant referral.
  3. No retroactive referral claims after purchase without a pre-existing accepted and timestamped lead registration; no double commission, code transfer, coupon stacking or self-attribution.
  4. One initial verified purchase and eligible paid upsells/renewals occurring within 12 months of that first purchase may qualify. There is no lifetime, automatic renewal or multi-level commission promise.

4. Financial year, sales base and annual tiers

The qualifying year is 1 April through 31 March, Indian time. Eligible net revenue means actual successfully captured and settled INR invoice proceeds, after discounts, credits, refunds and chargebacks and excluding GST/indirect taxes. Payment-processor charges are paid by the operator and do not reduce the customer's eligible pre-tax invoice amount. Trial, unpaid, failed, cancelled, self-referral and excluded product orders are ineligible.

Retroactive annual percentage

  • Starter: 20% when annual eligible net sales are below ₹5,00,000.
  • Growth: 25% when annual eligible net sales are ₹5,00,000 to below ₹10,00,000.
  • Elite: 30% when annual eligible net sales are at least ₹10,00,000.

Once a milestone is verified, the percentage applies across all eligible net revenue in that financial year. At each monthly review, previously earned commission is compared with the newly verified milestone rate and a retroactive reconciliation credit is recorded. The final year-end review corrects any remaining adjustments. Unverified future sales never count toward a milestone. Thresholds reset each 1 April; adjustments to the prior year may be made for refunds or fraud.

5. When commissions are credited

No credit is created without gateway-confirmed capture and settlement, verified product licence or delivery, a valid accepted referral, exclusion checks, unique payment/event identifiers and a cleared return/chargeback review. The standard hold is at least 45 calendar days after successful fulfilment and settlement. Longer payment disputes, customer claims or fraud concerns extend the hold. Commission balances are estimates until approved by finance.

6. Payout schedule and verification

  1. Finance prepares a monthly commission statement and a proposed payout run on the 20th for cleared, approved commission balances, subject to banking days and legal compliance.
  2. The release threshold is ₹2,000 of available approved commission. Smaller positive balances roll forward. No partner joining or payout release fees are charged.
  3. Bank payout goes only to an account verified in the partner's own name or lawful business name. Collect PAN, payment information, and supporting KYC through a secure separately authenticated process after acceptance, never via the public application or email.
  4. Where applicable, the partner submits a valid invoice with GST information. The operator validates tax status and deducts/deposits TDS under applicable law. The gross commission, tax invoice, tax withholding, net remittance and transaction reference appear separately.
  5. Two different authorised finance persons independently approve every payout batch, with segregation between calculation, beneficiary edits, approval and release. Changes in beneficiary details require a second verification and temporary payout hold.
  6. Milestone top-ups are reviewed at monthly release cycles. Remaining retroactive year-end top-ups or downward adjustments are finalised within 90 days after 31 March, subject to settled records, tax clearance and pending refund disputes. Entries are not silently rewritten after payout: they generate traceable adjustment/reversal records.

7. Fraud, reversals and audit trail

Suspicious, duplicate or inconsistent sales can be placed on hold while investigated. Refunds, chargebacks, order cancellation, misuse, or ineligible procurement reverse the attributable commission. Amounts already paid may be offset from future balances; any agreed lawful recovery is separately recorded. The operator preserves order IDs, settled base value, attribution evidence, approval identities, tax documents, invoice references, reversal reasons and payout references for required accounting and audit retention. Partners receive only their own financial statement—not customer complaint, witness, inquiry or other personal case data.

8. Restricted promotion and ethics

Partners must use accurate approved descriptions, disclose their financial incentive where required, avoid unsolicited or unlawful spam, impersonation, public-sector/government logo use, unverifiable certifications, guarantees of inquiry outcomes, bribes, procurement inducements, claims of NCW/Bar Council/government endorsement, employer/IC/LC conflicts and collection of sensitive complaint details. Referral compensation cannot be used to solicit or share regulated advocate professional fees.

9. Governing records, suspension and disputes

All referral claims are subject to the secure operator ledger. Partner statements may be disputed within 30 days of publication, with relevant evidence and no confidential case information. Misrepresentation or fraud may result in immediate suspension; ordinary curable breaches may receive written notice and an opportunity to rectify. Valid accrued commissions remain subject to refunds, tax and applicable contractual or legal set-off. Future programme changes require reasonable advance notice and do not extinguish already verified, earned commissions. Written signed terms and applicable law prevail if inconsistent with this preview.

10. Statutory tax guidance

For resident commission/brokerage payments falling within Income-tax Act, 2025, Section 393(1), Table for Payments to Resident, serial 1(ii), the published rate is 2% subject to the stated ₹20,000 threshold and applicable payer rules. The older Section 194H terminology applies to periods governed by the Income-tax Act, 1961, not to new post-1 April 2026 transactions. Actual withholding, GST registration, invoicing, nonresident treatment and other obligations must be reviewed by the operator's finance/tax adviser for each partner.

Income Tax Department: Section 393 · Ministry of Law & Justice: advocate marketing restrictions · CBIC: GST registration law

11. Privacy and contact

Partner applications request only professional contact and marketing-channel details. Tax identification and bank documents, when required, will be requested through a separate protected onboarding method. The operator may contact applicants about their submission; promotional mailing requires a distinct lawful basis. For questions or to request correction/deletion where applicable, email ankur.attorneyatlaw@gmail.com. See the privacy notice.
